newsitem.title: UK: Rifkind to challenge Germany on EU integration.
newsitem.headline: Rifkind to challenge Germany on EU integration.

text.p: Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind will issue a direct challenge to Chancellor Helmut Kohl on Wednesday to spell out the limits Germany sees to further integration of the European Union, British officials said on Tuesday.
Rifkind will travel to Bonn for meetings with German politicians and to make the second in a series of speeches setting out Britain's vision of a flexible Europe of freely cooperating nation states.

Although Kohl insists he is opposed to the emergence of a European superstate, Rifkind will argue that some elements of Germany's negotiating stance in the inter-governmental conference on the future shape of the EU suggest the opposite.
"It will be a serious speech intended to engage the Germans intellectually," one official said.

Rifkind will ask Germany to square its rejection of a United States of Europe with its proposals to extend majority voting within the EU to areas of foreign policy, to bring subjects such as immigration under the umbrella of the EU and to give more power to the European Parliament.
Transferring even more powers from national parliaments to the institutions of the EU could entail serious democratic risks, Rifkind will tell his German hosts.

Although the foreign secretary's remarks are potentially controversial, his aides said they were well timed to coincide with the stirrings of a debate in Germany -- spurred by rising unemployment and the approach of the single currency -- on the economic and political course the 15-nation bloc should take.
Rifkind summed up Britain's views in the first of his programme of speeches in Stockholm on February 3.

"Britain's vision is not anti-European. We believe that closer cooperation in Europe is in all our interests. But it must be done in a way which reflects the reality of what our citizens feel comfortable with," he said.
